subject: Error "Terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std:: logical error' what(): Mat:: operator(): index out of bounds."

messages.author: 6e7728addc65d294
messages.subject: Error "Terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std:: logical error' what(): Mat:: operator(): index out of bounds."
parts:
Hi Group,

I am running occupancy models for five species in two sites. I have five covariates for each site that impact occupancy and two that impact detection. I am using unmarked and quite new to it. I am trying to run three models first [p(effort).psi(.), p(human disturbance)psi(.) and p(effort, human disturbance).psi(.)] to set the covariates for detection (p) with fixed occupancy (psi) before running the actual occupancy models. The models run perfectly when there is only the covariate "effort" on it but when I put "human disturbance" in the model I get an error 

Terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std:: logical error' what(): Mat:: operator(): index out of bounds.

A window appears with a note that R encountered a fatal error and it needs to close. I lose all my models and it starts again. 

I already ran 64 models from another site and they did perfectly well even with human disturbance covariate (except for some NaNs errors). I checked my data and it seems fine. I tried to create another excel file with data to see if there is a problem in the file but it did not work. I looked in google but I did not understand. Does anyone in this group has any sort of idea how did it happen and what can be done? 

Yadav Ghimirey
Oxford, UK

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error "Terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std:: logical error' what(): Mat:: operator(): index out of bounds."
parts:
That's not good. Can you show a summary of the data and the code you used to fit the model? The results of sessionInfo() might be useful too.

The error is coming from the C++ code, so one quick fix is to use the R code instead:

occu(..., engine="R")


Richard
